Subject: EU-only processing — request for deletion evidence and attestation

Hi Marcus,

Thanks for taking this on. As part of our procurement & privacy review we need confirmation that EuroHealth customer data can be processed exclusively in EU physical locations under the Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) and, critically, we need an auditable "proof of deletion" path for records once retention expires.

Specifically we would like:
- A short description of how Redwood enforces EU-only processing (routing, control plane, logging).
- Sample deletion logs / job artifacts showing hard delete timestamps and scope (preferably a CSV sample).
- Clarification on whether any metadata or backups are ever transferred outside the EU when SCCs are in place.
- Whether keys are customer-managed in Private offerings and how KMS owners are recorded.
- A short attestation template or certificate your legal team would sign confirming deletion actions were taken.

We need this evidence to close our privacy review by 2026-11-05. Can you confirm owners and an ETA?

Best,
Anouk
Anouk Muller
Head of Privacy — EuroHealth

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: EU-only processing — request for deletion evidence and attestation

Marcus / team — summary below and attachments. Attaching: EU_SCCs_Processing_Summary.pdf, Deletion_Log_Sample.csv (redacted), plus an internal checklist.

Key points:
1) EU-only processing
- Hosted API: we support region routing so customer workloads can be pinned to EU regions; control plane metadata remains in the control plane that can be configured for EU-only in our Private offering. We implement SCCs for transfers where applicable.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): we support customer-managed KMS. For Private deployments the customer retains sole key custody when requested.

2) Backups & metadata transfers
- Backups are region-scoped for EU-only deployments. We do not replicate EU-only customer data to outside regions unless explicitly requested (audit trail is available showing replication decisions). Metadata necessary for routing (non-content) may be stored in control plane; we document what is stored in EU_SCCs_Processing_Summary.pdf.

3) Deletion and proof artifacts
- Deletion is performed by a scheduled purge job; the job emits a deletion manifest containing: object id, deletion timestamp (UTC), retention policy id, and purge job run id. Sample manifest attached (Deletion_Log_Sample.csv).
- For redundancy, we record both the purge operation and the verification scrub. For physical media, we track the snapshot lifecycle and deletion dates.

Questions for EuroHealth:
- Do you need evidence at the record-level (per object) or is an aggregate run manifest sufficient?
- Will attachments (user-uploaded files) and audio transcripts be in scope? Those typically live in object storage and follow the same purge pipeline but we want to confirm scope.

ETA: If we get scope today, we can prepare an attestation package + redacted logs by 2026-11-04.

—Naomi
Senior Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Anouk Muller <anouk.muller@eurohealth.com>

Date: 2026-10-24T15:03:00+01:00
Subject: Re: EU-only processing — request for deletion evidence and attestation

Thanks Naomi — that helps. A couple of clarifications from our side:

- We need per-object deletion evidence for a 30-day window following a retention expiration event for a random sample (audit purposes). Aggregate manifests are useful, but our privacy office insists on object-level timestamps for samples.
- Scope: user profile data and attachments (files) are in scope. Audio transcripts are not in scope for this engagement.
- KMS: for Private deployments we do want customer-managed keys; for hosted API we'll expect Redwood to confirm whether CMK is possible or if only Redwood-managed keys are offered for hosted customers.

Timeline: evidence required by 2026-11-05 for the procurement packet. Please treat the attestation wording as something we may include in legal review, so Kim's input is critical.

Best,
Anouk
